title: curl: new option --status return http status code
body:
# New Option `--status` Proposal

This PR proposes a new `--status` option that simplifies the below use case.
It does one thing: output only the HTTP status code of the requested URL.

## Use Case

Performing a web search like "curl get last status code" yields results like:

- Getting curl to output HTTP status code?
- How to Get the HTTP Status of a Site Using cURL
- Return only a HTTP status code from curl command

The same occurs when searching for something like "command line tool get http 
status code only".

Currently, the solutions involve complex command combinations like:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://www.example.com
curl -LI http://www.example.com -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -s
```

or using pipes:

```bash
curl -sI http://www.example.com | sed -n 's/^HTTP[^ ]* \([0-9][0-9][0-9]\).*/\1/p'
```

So I thought - why not have `curl` do this one thing without having to memorize 
a combination of options, or pipe the output to `sed` in order to get just the
http status code.

This is particularly useful in shell scripts and automation when you only need
to check the HTTP response status without processing the full response.

## Example usage:

```bash
curl --status -s https://example.com
# Outputs: 200

curl -s --status curl.se
# Outputs: 301

curl -sL --status curl.se
# Outputs: 202
```

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+---
+c: Copyright (C) Daniel Stenberg, <daniel@haxx.se>, et al.
+SPDX-License-Identifier: curl
+Long: status
+Help: Output only the HTTP status code
+Protocols: HTTP HTTPS
+Category: http
+Added: 8.18.0
+Multi: boolean
+See-also:
+  - head
+  - location
+  - show-headers
+  - silent
+  - verbose
+Example:
+  - --status $URL
+---
+
+# `--status`
+
+Output only the HTTP status code from the response. This option suppresses all
+other output including headers and response body, displaying only the numeric
+HTTP status code (e.g., 200, 404, 500).
+
+When combined with --silent, this produces clean output with only the status
+code.
+
+Combine with --location to get the status code for the redirect.

+<testcase>
+<info>
+<keywords>
+HTTPS
+HTTP GET
+--status
+</keywords>
+</info>
+
+#
+# Server-side
+<reply>
+<data nocheck="yes">
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2010 14:49:00 GMT
+Server: test-server/fake
+Content-Length: 6
+
+hello
+</data>
+</reply>
+
+#
+# Client-side
+<client>
+<features>
+SSL
+</features>
+<server>
+https
+</server>
+<name>
+HTTPS GET with --status (status code only output)
+</name>
+<command option="no-include">
+--status -k https://%HOSTIP:%HTTPSPORT/%TESTNUMBER
+</command>
+</client>
+
+#
+# Verify data after the test has been "shot"
+<verify>
+<protocol crlf="headers">
+GET /%TESTNUMBER HTTP/1.1
+Host: %HOSTIP:%HTTPSPORT
+User-Agent: curl/%VERSION
+Accept: */*
+
+</protocol>
+<stdout>
+200
+</stdout>
+</verify>
+</testcase>
